                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"
                if mkdir -p "$STALE_DIR" 2>/dev/null && mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" "$STALE_DIR/" 2>/dev/null; then
                  mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
                else
                  echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
                fi
              else
                mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
              fi
            done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          if [ -d "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" ]; then
            echo "Restoring macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf build/macos 2>/dev/null || true
            mkdir -p build
            mv "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" build/ \
              || echo "::warning::could not restore the $ARCH build cache — it will be rebuilt from scratch (gh-1600)"
          fi

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): same rationale as
      # build-mobile.yml — on a persistent self-hosted runner the
      # flutter-action cache costs a ~1GB untar on setup plus a whole-SDK
      # re-tar POST per job. The composite action pins the SDK at
      # ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk (.fah-version marker):
      # subsecond reuse, one download per pin bump, no POST step.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install instead of the runner's
      # pre-installed SDK — the candidate-path loop picked up a stale
      # 3.44.4 at ~/.local/flutter, which broke `flutter pub get` the
      # moment the repo floor moved to >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260/#261).
      - name: Setup Flutter environment
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          # EXACT patch pin (#1431): this leg builds + gates fa-extension.zip
          # against scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv — a wildcard pin
          # re-resolves a new engine build on every 3.47.x patch and moves
          # the canvaskit/skwasm rev-hash dir the gate tracks. Bump
          # consciously, with any floor reseed in the same PR.
          #
          # 3.47.7 (gh-1814, reverting the #1813 3.47.4 pin): 3.47.4 was
          # the last patch honoring FLUTTER_SWIFT_PACKAGE_MANAGER=0, but it
          # is UNREACHABLE here — the fa-m5 runners' ~60kB/s link cannot
          # download that SDK (run 40034163885 died in the download, bounded
          # retries exhausted) — and with the SPM lane adopted (see the job
          # env comment above) there is no reason to chase it: 3.47.7's
          # forced SPM integration is now the lane, its floor bump verified
          # working (`generated floor: 14.0` in the run 40022900373 gate
          # diagnostic), and scripts/assert_macos_min_platform.sh asserts
          # the post-config state. Same 3.47.7 the extension + Pages legs
          # already pin.
          flutter-version: '3.47.7'

      - name: Setup host toolchains
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          flutter --version
          dart --version

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        run: |
          if command -v rustup &> /dev/null; then
            echo "Rust already installed"
            rustup show
          else
            echo "Installing Rust..."
            curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y
            source "$HOME/.cargo/env"
          fi
          echo "$HOME/.cargo/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          rustup --version
          cargo --version

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The plist is gitignored, so the fresh CI checkout has none and the
      # native Firebase SDK logs I-COR000012/0008 at startup. Inject it from
      # a secret when available (same dev.fa1.app registration as
      # firebase_options.dart).
      - name: Write GoogleService-Info.plist (macOS)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/macos/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist
            echo "GoogleService-Info.plist written (bundle: $(plutil -extract BUNDLE_ID raw flutter_app/macos/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist))"
          else
            echo "⚠️ GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64 not set — building without the native Firebase plist"
          fi

      - name: Install Flutter dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: Dependency versions
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          echo "=== Dependency versions ==="
          flutter pub deps --style=compact

      # full pod install (~4 min with Firebase). Cache it keyed by the
      # lockfile; $HOME-level caches (pub-cache, CocoaPods download cache,
      # Ruby gems, Flutter SDK) already persist on the self-hosted runner.
      - name: Cache CocoaPods (macOS)

        with:
          path: flutter_app/macos/Pods
          key: macos-pods-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/macos/Podfile.lock') }}

      - name: Generate build info
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          GIT_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
          GIT_BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)

          mkdir -p lib/core/services
          printf '%s\n' \
            '// Generated build info — CI overwrites this file before compilation.' \
            '// ignore_for_file: constant_identifier_names' \
            '' \
            "const String kBuildGitCommit = '${GIT_COMMIT}';" \
            "const String kBuildGitBranch = '${GIT_BRANCH}';" \

      - name: Cache vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework
          key: wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0
      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 20
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Order of preference:
          # 1) actions/cache hit (keyed by the release tag) — warm until the
          #    repo's daily cache churn LRU-evicts the entry (saved 10-20
          #    06:02Z, gone by 10-21 19:03Z: gh-1759 ran cold twice);
          # 2) local working copy on this self-hosted runner;
          # 3) upstream release asset — the curl budget MUST fit the step
          #    cap WITH CORRECT ARITHMETIC (gh-1149): retries live in THIS
          #    bash loop, not curl --retry (which adds N MORE attempts AND
          #    restarts+truncates instead of resuming). Worst case with the
          #    gh-1759 budget: 4 × 240s max-time + 3 × 5s sleeps = 975s,
          #    + connect + unzip + slack ≈ 1035s < the 20-min (1200s) cap.
          #
          #    gh-1759: the gh-1149 budget (3 × 240s) was sized for this
          #    link's good-day ~300KB/s. The 10-21 daily run measured
          #    40–108KB/s (cold cache, both arch jobs): 3 × 240s banked
          #    only 29.5MB (x86_64) / 73% (arm64) of the 97,238,501-byte
          #    asset and the leg went red. Resume worked (`Resuming
          #    transfer from byte position …` in the logs) — the wire
          #    budget was simply too small, and the old pre-loop wipe
          #    threw each run's partial away, so a slow-link day never
          #    banked durable progress and the leg could not self-heal.
          #    Fixes: (a) the per-arch /tmp partial now PERSISTS across
          #    runs — -C - resumes it within the step AND across daily
          #    runs (macOS prunes only 3-day-untouched /tmp files; a daily
          #    run touches it) until the asset completes and the
          #    actions/cache post-step saves the framework; (b) the loop
          #    grew to 4 × 240s under a 20-min step cap.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks"
          # PER-ARCH zip path: both matrix archs run on ONE self-hosted
          # runner (the shared-state race this file already guards with
          # per-arch keychains below) — a shared arch-less /tmp zip would
          # let one job's cleanup unlink the other's in-flight partial,
          # then both curls interleave bytes into one path.
          ZIP="/tmp/WasmRun.xcframework-${{ matrix.arch }}.zip"
          # The release asset is immutable per tag — pin its digest so a
          # wrong-content-but-valid-zip cannot slip past unzip CRC32 into
          # the permanent wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0 cache. The pinned byte size tells a
          # truncated download (KEEP the partial — the next run resumes
          # it) apart from a complete-but-wrong one (PURGE and restart).
          ASSET_DIGEST="aca903d732202bcdf9c8d19fbb8a795c3c930762419f852a5ee228468c548a98"
          ASSET_BYTES=97238501
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -f "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework/Info.plist" ]; then
            echo "Using framework already in place (actions/cache hit or valid leftover)"
          elif [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "No cache, no local copy — downloading from upstream release..."
            # The partial is deliberately NOT deleted between runs
            # (gh-1759): it is exactly what -C - is for. If the persisted
            # zip is already complete AND digest-valid, skip the download
            # — a -C - attempt against a complete file gets HTTP 416 and
            # reads success as failure.
            if [ -f "$ZIP" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Complete, digest-valid $ZIP persisted from an earlier run — skipping download"
            else
              for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
                # --fail: without it curl exits 0 on HTTP 404/5xx and writes
                # the error page into the zip; with it every HTTP error
                # engages this loop's retries. -C - makes each attempt
                # RESUME the partial zip (Range requests), so slow links
                # make forward progress within this step AND across runs.
                if curl --fail -L -C - --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 240 \
                  -o "$ZIP" \
                  https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip; then
                  break
                fi
                if [ "$attempt" = "4" ]; then
                  echo "download attempt $attempt failed — out of loop attempts" >&2
                else
                  echo "download attempt $attempt failed, resuming in 5s..."
                  sleep 5
                fi
              done
              got=$(wc -c < "$ZIP" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || echo 0)
              if [ "$got" -eq "$ASSET_BYTES" ] && echo "$ASSET_DIGEST  $ZIP" | shasum -a 256 -c -; then
                : # complete and authentic — fall through to unzip
              elif [ "$got" -lt "$ASSET_BYTES" ]; then
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip incomplete: $got / $ASSET_BYTES bytes after $attempt attempts — keeping the partial; the next run resumes from byte $got (gh-1759)" >&2
                exit 1
              else
                echo "WasmRun.xcframework.zip is $got bytes (expected $ASSET_BYTES) or failed its pinned sha256 — purging it so the next run restarts clean" >&2
                rm -f "$ZIP"
                exit 1
              fi
            fi
            unzip -q "$ZIP" -d "$DEST"
          fi
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      # Per-arch keychain: both matrix archs build on ONE self-hosted
      # runner; a shared build.keychain raced (one job's delete+create
      # emptied it under the other's codesign — errSecInternalComponent /
      # "No certificate found", builds 86).
      - name: Provision signing via ci-sign (persistent host keychain)
        id: signing
        env:
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
          CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV: MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64
          CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV: MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD
          MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          # gh-1865: the repo copy of ci-sign is authoritative —
          # re-install it to the host PATH on every signing job so
          # ~/bin/ci-sign can never drift from the reviewed source.
          # gh-1954: install(1) does not create parent directories —
          # on a fresh runner $HOME/bin does not exist (run 40822964468,
          # "install: invalid target .../bin/ci-sign: No such file").
          # gh-2030: this install used to live ONLY in the ubuntu-latest
          # `version` job, which never executes ci-sign — the one job that
          # runs it on the signing hosts (this one) never refreshed the
          # copy, so fa-m5 executed a stale pre-gh-2008 script whose
          # set-keychain-settings still raised orphan SecurityAgent dialogs
          # and wedged the x86_64 `security import` for 2h27m (run
          # 41276487426: "User canceled the operation"). Same shape the
          # build-mobile.yml iOS signing step has always used.
          mkdir -p "$HOME/bin"
          install -m 755 scripts/ci-sign "$HOME/bin/ci-sign"
          if [ -z "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "⚠️  No signing certificate found — building unsigned (development only)"
            signed=false
            echo "signed=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            signed=true
            echo "✅ Signing certificate found — provisioning via ci-sign..."
            # gh-1865 model v3 (owner decision 2026-10-28): NO per-arch
            # temporary keychains, NO search-list writes, NO default-keychain
            # flips. ~/bin/ci-sign keeps the PERSISTENT ci-signing.keychain-db
            # provisioned (idempotent — concurrent matrix legs re-verify in
            # milliseconds) and pins the identity by SHA-1, so a concurrent
            # leg's same-subject certificate (gh-1865, run 40455401630)
            # cannot shadow resolution. The old per-arch keychain
            # delete+create race was gh-1852; the eviction race was gh-1866;
            # both classes are structurally gone.
            ~/bin/ci-sign install fa-macos
            CERT_SHA1=$(~/bin/ci-sign sha1 fa-macos)
            CERT_NAME=$(~/bin/ci-sign name fa-macos)
            echo "identity_sha1=$CERT_SHA1" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "identity_name=$CERT_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "gh-1865: signing identity pinned by SHA-1: $CERT_NAME ($CERT_SHA1)"
            echo "signed=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

          if [ -n "$MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64" | base64 --decode > profile.provisionprofile
            echo "profile_embedded=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

            # Make the profile visible to Xcode manual signing. Decoding
            # goes through ci-sign plist — the legacy CMS decoder needs a
            # default keychain, which this model never sets.
            PROFILE_UUID=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract UUID raw -)
            PROFILE_NAME=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract Name raw -)
            PROFILE_TEAM=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract TeamIdentifier.0 raw - 2>/dev/null || true)
            echo "Profile: $PROFILE_NAME / UUID: $PROFILE_UUID / team: $PROFILE_TEAM"
            mkdir -p "$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles"
            cp profile.provisionprofile "$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles/${PROFILE_UUID}.provisionprofile"
            echo "profile_uuid=$PROFILE_UUID" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "profile_team=$PROFILE_TEAM" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

            # gh-1865 fail-fast precheck (owner option B): the profile must
            # embed the provisioned certificate — a mismatch aborts here in
            # seconds instead of surfacing as a dead archive after the full
            # build. Skipped on unsigned runs (no provisioned cert).
            if [ -n "${CERT_SHA1:-}" ]; then
              ~/bin/ci-sign doctor profile.provisionprofile fa-macos
            fi
          else
            echo "⚠️  No provisioning profile found — TestFlight will warn"
            echo "profile_embedded=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi
          # gh-1986: keychain re-unlock WATCHDOG for the whole signing
          # window. The persistent ci-signing.keychain-db auto-locks after
          # ~5 min of inactivity, and `set-keychain-settings -t 0` cannot
          # fix it non-interactively on this host (GUI SecurityAgent
          # prompt — screenshot-confirmed in the Fastfile; ci-sign's
          # bounded attempt is alarm-killed: "Alarm clock: 14" in this
          # step's log). gh-1954's --force host re-provision (run
          # 40857357741, 2026-10-29) re-created the keychain with the
          # locking defaults, and this leg — unlike the iOS gym lane —
          # had no unlock watchdog: run 41008008179 (gh-1986) then hit its
          # FIRST codesign 2h14m after this step's unlock and BOTH matrix
          # archs died with errSecInternalComponent on the same embedded
          # framework (GoogleAppMeasurement), 0.4 s apart. Same fix
          # gh-1954 gave gym: re-unlock every 60 s (unlock-keychain -p
          # never prompts) across build, DMG/PKG packaging, notarize and
          # the no-sandbox build; the always() Cleanup step stops it.
          if [ "$signed" = "true" ]; then
            ~/bin/ci-sign unlock
            nohup bash -c 'while :; do sleep 60; ~/bin/ci-sign unlock >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done' \
              </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
            disown
            echo $! > ci-sign-watchdog.pid
            echo "ci-sign unlock watchdog armed (pid $(cat ci-sign-watchdog.pid), 60s cadence — gh-1986)"
          fi

      - name: Build macOS release (${{ matrix.arch }})
        env:
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          BUILD_VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          # gh-1865: CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY as a SHA-1 fingerprint (read from
          # THIS job's own keychain right after import) instead of the
          # name-based MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID secret — a concurrent signing
          # leg's same-CN cert in the shared additive search list can no
          # longer shadow the identity at codesign time.
          CERT_SHA1: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.identity_sha1 }}
          MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID }}
          PROFILE_UUID: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_uuid }}
          PROFILE_TEAM: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_team }}
        run: |
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          echo "Building for architecture: $ARCH"
          cd flutter_app
          if [ -n "${CERT_SHA1:-}" ]; then
            export FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="$CERT_SHA1"
            export FA_CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual
            if [ -n "${MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID:-}" ]; then
              export FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID"
            elif [ -n "${PROFILE_TEAM:-}" ]; then
              export FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$PROFILE_TEAM"
            fi
            if [ -n "${PROFILE_UUID:-}" ]; then
              export FA_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER="$PROFILE_UUID"
            fi
          else
            export FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="-"
            export FA_CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic
          fi
          # gh-1814 REG gate — fail loud at build time, not at release time.
          # --config-only drives the tool's real SPM/pods config pass
          # (the SwiftPM migration + pod install) without compiling; the
          # gate then ASSERTS the adopted SPM lane: SwiftPM state EXPECTED
          # after the config pass (pbxproj marker + ephemeral generated
          # package), app floor 14.0 (pbxproj + Podfile), generated package
          # floor ≥ 14.0 (the tool's silent showBuildSettings bump must
          # have landed — the literal gh-180 killer), no SwiftPM product
          # above the app min, and the vendored inappwebview manifest
          # floored at 14.0 if it ever reappears. A drift fails in seconds
          # with the remediation instead of Xcode's cryptic "requires
          # minimum platform version" error after a 50+-minute resolution
          # pass (gh-1798 measured 3365s on the first Xcode 27 run).
          # gh-1800 follow-up (the residue clean stays): self-hosted
          # workdirs are PERSISTENT — untracked build state (macos/Flutter/
          # ephemeral, Pods, .symlinks) survives actions/checkout, so it is
          # wiped before every build and the config-only pass regenerates a
          # DETERMINISTIC fresh SPM migration + pod install (the pre-#1812
          # runs showed stale residue steering the lane). The gate below
          # then sees exactly the state a fresh 3.47.7 config pass
          # produces.
          flutter clean
          rm -rf macos/Flutter/ephemeral macos/Pods macos/.symlinks
          FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS="$ARCH" flutter build macos --config-only
          bash ../scripts/assert_macos_min_platform.sh 14.0
          FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS="$ARCH" flutter build macos --release \
            --build-name=$BUILD_VERSION \
            --build-number=$BUILD_NUMBER
          MAIN_BIN=$(find build/macos/Build/Products/Release/Fa.app -name "Fa" -type f | head -1)
          echo "=== Binary architecture verification ==="
          echo "Binary path: $MAIN_BIN"
          file "$MAIN_BIN"
          lipo -info "$MAIN_BIN"
          echo "=== End binary verification ==="
          # The Dart side resolves the wasm_run FFI surface via dlsym on the
          # main executable. If the symbols were dead-stripped or not exported
          # the app boots to a white screen on TestFlight — fail here instead.
          echo "=== wasm_run FFI symbol verification ==="
          # dyld_info reads the exports trie, which survives stripping
          # (nm -gD fails on stripped binaries with "no dynamic symbol table").
          EXPORTS=$(xcrun dyld_info -exports "$MAIN_BIN" 2>/dev/null || true)
          WIRE_COUNT=$(echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -c " _wire_" || true)
          echo "wasm_run wire_* exports in binary: $WIRE_COUNT"
          for SYM in _wire_compile_wasm _store_dart_post_cobject _init_frb_dart_api_dl; do
            if ! echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -qE " ${SYM}\$"; then
              echo "::error::$SYM is not exported from the app binary — wasm_run would crash at runtime (white screen)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "✅ wasm_run FFI symbols are exported"

      - name: Package as DMG
        id: package
        env:
          SIGNED: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.signed }}
          PROFILE_EMBEDDED: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_embedded }}
          # gh-1865: sign by SHA-1 fingerprint (name-based MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID
          # is a lottery when a concurrent leg's same-CN cert sits in the
          # shared additive search list). CERT_NAME keys the already-signed
          # skip check — `codesign -dv` prints the Authority CN, never the
          # SHA-1.
          CERT_SHA1: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.identity_sha1 }}
          CERT_NAME: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.identity_name }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          APP_PATH="flutter_app/build/macos/Build/Products/Release/Fa.app"
          DMG_NAME="fa-macos-${ARCH}-${VERSION}.dmg"

          # Size diet (#1096 AC4 + direction 3): drop what no macOS code path
          # can load — before any codesign so the seal covers the shipped
          # tree. Both cuts ride in flutter_assets inside App.framework:
          # 1) assets/wasm (~47 MB) — WASI interpreter modules loaded
          #    exclusively via WasiSandboxShell (env_factory_io.dart routes
          #    desktops to the host Process shell; every rootBundle.load of
          #    assets/wasm lives in the mobile-only shell).
          # 2) packages/js_widget_runtime/test — the pub package's
          #    own test fixture (coach_anny.glb, 5.6 MB); nothing in the app
          #    references that path (the live model, when used, is fetched
          #    by the JS-app catalog, not bundled).
          ASSETS="$APP_PATH/Contents/Frameworks/App.framework/Versions/A/Resources/flutter_assets"
          # Shared prune (scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh — the same call
          # runs on the no-sandbox build and every web packaging surface):
          # fails loudly if the flutter_assets layout drifts instead of
          # silently shipping the fat bundle. Re-enable path (review,
          # #1096): if a desktop WASI/sandbox mode ever ships
          # (WasiSandboxShell on macOS), reseed assets/wasm — until then a
          # desktop wasm load would fail as a missing asset, not a
          # #1224-class "no lazy loader" stub.
          bash scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh "$ASSETS" \
            assets/wasm packages/js_widget_runtime/test

          rm -f fa-macos-*.dmg tmp-fa.dmg
          rm -rf dmg-staging

          echo "Packaging: $APP_PATH → $DMG_NAME (arch: $ARCH)"

          if [ "$SIGNED" = "true" ] && [ -n "$CERT_SHA1" ]; then
            echo "Signing .app bundle..."

            RESVG_BIN="$APP_PATH/Contents/Resources/resvg"
            if [ -f "$RESVG_BIN" ]; then
              echo "Stripping extended attributes from resvg..."
              xattr -cr "$RESVG_BIN" 2>/dev/null || true
              echo "Signing resvg binary..."
              codesign --force --sign "$CERT_SHA1" \
                --options runtime \
                --timestamp \
                "$RESVG_BIN"
            fi

            find "$APP_PATH" -type f \( -perm +111 -o -name '*.dylib' \) | while read -r bin; do
              if codesign -dv "$bin" 2>/dev/null | grep -qF "$CERT_NAME"; then
                continue
              fi
              echo "Signing nested binary: $bin"
              codesign --force --sign "$CERT_SHA1" \
                --options runtime \
                --timestamp \
                "$bin" 2>/dev/null || true
            done

            if [ "$PROFILE_EMBEDDED" = "true" ] && [ -f "profile.provisionprofile" ]; then
              echo "Embedding provisioning profile..."
              cp profile.provisionprofile "$APP_PATH/Contents/embedded.provisionprofile"
              # gh-1865 model v3: profile decoding via ci-sign plist —
              # the legacy CMS decoder needs a default keychain, which this
              # model never sets.
              APP_ID=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract Entitlements xml1 -o - - | grep -A 1 'com.apple.application-identifier' | tail -1 | sed 's/.*<string>\(.*\)<\/string>.*/\1/')
              TEAM_ID="${APP_ID%%.*}"
              # Start from Release.entitlements (network client+server, file
              # bookmarks, calendar, contacts, health, homekit, audio input)
              # and inject the provisioning identity keys — do NOT collapse
              # to a sandbox-only dict: the app needs every entitlement the
              # sandbox declares, and dropping them breaks SSO callback
              # servers, file access, and OS-level permission flows in the
              # signed production build.
              cp flutter_app/macos/Runner/Release.entitlements entitlements.plist
              # PlistBuddy handles dotted top-level key names (plutil
              # -insert/-replace treats dots as nested key separators).
              /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Add :com.apple.application-identifier string $APP_ID" entitlements.plist
              /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Add :com.apple.developer.team-identifier string $TEAM_ID" entitlements.plist
              # The profile may not grant every *capability* the app declares
              # (e.g. homekit needs a separate App ID capability in the
              # Developer Portal). TestFlight rejects capability entitlements
              # the profile doesn't include ('Invalid Code Signing
              # Entitlements', error 90285).
              #
              # Only com.apple.developer.* keys are profile-gated. The
              # com.apple.security.* sandbox entitlements (network, files,
              # personal-information) are NOT in the profile by design — any
              # sandboxed app may declare them — so they must survive.
              #
              # NOTE: `plutil -extract ... -o -` (stdout form) is not
              # supported on every macOS the runner may have; use real temp
              # files so the extraction can't silently produce nothing.
              ~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile > profile_decoded.plist
              plutil -extract Entitlements json profile_decoded.plist -o profile_ents.json
              for KEY in $(plutil -convert xml1 entitlements.plist -o - | grep -o '<key>[^<]*</key>' | sed 's/<[^>]*>//g'); do
                case "$KEY" in
                  com.apple.application-identifier|com.apple.developer.team-identifier) continue ;;
                  com.apple.developer.*) ;;
                  *) continue ;; # sandbox + misc entitlements are not profile-gated
                esac
                if ! python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('profile_ents.json')); raise SystemExit(0 if '$KEY' in d else 1)"; then
                  echo "Dropping capability not granted by profile: $KEY"
                  /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Delete :$KEY" entitlements.plist
                fi
              done
              ENTITLEMENTS="entitlements.plist"
            else
              ENTITLEMENTS="flutter_app/macos/Runner/Release.entitlements"
            fi

            codesign_app() {
              codesign --force --deep --sign "$CERT_SHA1" \
                --options runtime \
                --timestamp \
                --entitlements "$ENTITLEMENTS" \
                "$APP_PATH"
            }

            for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
              if codesign_app; then
                break
              fi
              if [ "$attempt" = "5" ]; then
                echo "codesign failed after $attempt attempts"
                exit 1
              fi
              sleep_seconds=$((attempt * 30))
              echo "codesign failed, retrying in ${sleep_seconds}s (attempt $attempt/5)..."
              sleep "$sleep_seconds"
            done

            echo "Verifying code signature..."
            codesign -vv --deep --strict "$APP_PATH"
            spctl -a -vv "$APP_PATH" 2>/dev/null || true
          fi

          DMG_STAGING="dmg-staging"
          rm -rf "$DMG_STAGING"
          mkdir "$DMG_STAGING"
          cp -R "$APP_PATH" "$DMG_STAGING/"
          ln -s /Applications "$DMG_STAGING/Applications"

          TMP_DMG="tmp-fa.dmg"
          hdiutil create \
            -volname "Fa $VERSION" \
            -srcfolder "$DMG_STAGING" \
            -ov \
            -format UDRW \
            "$TMP_DMG"

          hdiutil convert "$TMP_DMG" -format UDZO -o "$DMG_NAME"
          rm -f "$TMP_DMG"
          rm -rf "$DMG_STAGING"

          echo "dmg_name=$DMG_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          ZIP_NAME="fa-macos-${ARCH}-${VERSION}-mac.zip"
          echo "Packaging ZIP for auto-update: $ZIP_NAME"
          ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc --keepParent "$APP_PATH" "$ZIP_NAME"
          SHA512=$(openssl dgst -sha512 -binary "$ZIP_NAME" | openssl base64 -A)
          SIZE=$(stat -f%z "$ZIP_NAME")
          MANIFEST_ARCH="$ARCH"
          if [ "$MANIFEST_ARCH" = "x86_64" ]; then
            MANIFEST_ARCH="x64"
          fi
          MANIFEST_NAME="latest-mac-${MANIFEST_ARCH}.yml"
          RELEASE_DATE=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z")
          printf '%s\n' \
            "version: ${VERSION}" \
            "files:" \
            "  - url: ${ZIP_NAME}" \
            "    sha512: ${SHA512}" \
            "    size: ${SIZE}" \

content.text:
# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo +
#                                 the /outlook add-in slice; gh-1684:
#                                 the extension zip moved to GitHub
#                                 Releases and is no longer site-hosted)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1477: 10m was the same time bomb as the derive-version jobs — a
    # full-history fetch under a 10m ceiling. 20m + the blobless filter
    # below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.changed }}
      next_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
      latest_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.latest_tag }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.pubspec_version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: daily_plan.sh reads tags / commit metadata / one file
          # at origin/main — never historical blobs. Blobless keeps full
          # tag/commit metadata without the blobs (the full fetch outgrew
          # the old 10m ceiling in the twin derive-version job, run
          # 38027695551).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

Now the real failure emerges. The actual failure is:

``
This failed (attepted to download https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases/download/sqlite3-3.9.1/libsqlite3.arm64.macos.dylib).
Building assets for package:sqlite3 failed.
Running build hooks failed.
##[error]Process completed with exit code 255.
``

for the CLI bundle, and:

``
Building assets for package:sqlite3 failed.
Target build_hooks failed: Error: Building native assets failed. See the logs for more details.
Failed to package .../flutter_app.
Command PhaseScriptExecution failed with a nonzero exit code
** BUILD FAILED **
``

So the root cause is the sqlite3 package build hook failing to download `libsqlite3.arm64.macos.dylib` from GitHub releases (sqlite3-3.9.1). The "exit code 0 but produced no further output" errors on the Swift compile targets appear to be noise (likely the Swift compile being killed as part of the whole build failing, or Xcode's build system reporting strange errors when sub-steps fail — actually those errors happen because the overall build was failing and the Swift compiler invocations were terminated).

The key failure: `sqlite3` native assets build hook: "This failed (attepted to download https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases/download/sqlite3-3.9.1/libsqlite3.arm64.macos.dylib)". Note the typo "attepted" is from the sqlite3 package's own error message.

So the sqlite3 package (native assets feature) downloads a prebuilt libsqlite3 dylib from GitHub releases at build time. The download failed — likely due to the slow network on the runner (the ~60kB/s link mentioned in comments), or rate limiting, or the release asset doesn't exist for sqlite3-3.9.1.

Let me get the full log around that failure to understand exactly why the download failed (404? timeout? checksum mismatch?).

1. `downloadIntoOutputDirectoryShared` → writes to `input.outputDirectoryShared/<library.dirname>/<libsqlite3.dylib>`. If an existing cached file has the right hash → reuse.
2. Otherwise fetch from GitHub: `https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases/download/$RELEASE_TAG/$FILENAME`.
3. `_fetchFromSource` throws `CouldNotDownloadException` when status != 200 ("Unexpected response code: 504 Gateway Time-out" — the CLI leg case).
4. `fetch` validates sha256; mismatch → `StateError('Hash of downloaded file $filename is $digest, expected $hash.')` — the macOS app leg case.

The macOS legs got hash `bef140a1a...` for BOTH arm64 and x64 — identical content. What content would GitHub return with status 200 that hashes identically for both requests? A proxy-injected error page, OR... wait. GitHub releases downloads redirect to objects.githubusercontent.com. HttpClient follows redirects by default. A 504 from the proxy edge would have been caught by the status check (that's what happened on the CLI leg). So the app legs got a 200 response with the SAME wrong body for both files. Hmm — that could be a captive-portal / Zscaler block page with 200, or a CDN "error" page.

@@ -0,0 +1,91 @@
+name: AAB 16k gate self-test
+
+# gh-798 AC3: the 16 KB page-size gate (scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh,
+# called by build-mobile.yml's "Verify AAB" step) is itself tested — a gate
+# that is wrong from day one (gh-786: APK-layout glob in an AAB) must be
+# caught at PR time, not by the nightly. This job runs the REAL gate script
+# against two fixture bundles:
+#   (a) libs present (a real 16 KB-aligned vendored .so under the AAB
+#       layout base/lib/<abi>/) → gate passes with the green marker;
+#   (b) libs absent → the named "::error:: expected native libs …"
+#       verdict, never a silent pass, never an inherited exit code.
+# A regressed glob or verdict turns this job red and blocks merge — the
+# fixture is the AAB layout, so ANY layout assumption regression fails
+# case (a) exactly like the nightly did (gh-786). A failure on an
+# unrelated change is the desired loudness — fix the gate or fixture,
+# never delete the job (gh-798 E3).
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    paths:
+      - '.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml'
+      - '.github/workflows/aab-gate-selftest.yml'
+      - 'scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh'
+      - 'scripts/patch_elf_16k_alignment.dart'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  self-test:
+    name: Gate self-test (fixture bundles)
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 15
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout repository
+        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
+      - name: Setup Flutter
+        # Only `dart` is needed (the 16 KB checker); flutter-action is the
+        # repo-standard pinned source of it and mirrors the real leg.
+        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
+        with:
+          channel: 'stable'
+          cache: true
+
+      - name: Build fixture bundles (AAB layout, with/without native libs)
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          # (a) with libs: a REAL 16 KB-aligned .so from the vendored
+          # wasm_run plugin, packaged at the AAB layout.
+          mkdir -p fx/with-libs/base/lib/arm64-v8a
+          cp vendor/wasm_run_flutter/android/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libwasm_run_dart.so fx/with-libs/base/lib/arm64-v8a/
+          (cd fx/with-libs && zip -q -r -X ../with-libs.aab base)
+          # (b) without libs: structurally valid bundle, zero native libs.
+          mkdir -p fx/without-libs/base
+          (cd fx/without-libs && zip -q -r -X ../without-libs.aab base)
+          unzip -l fx/with-libs.aab 'base/lib/*'
+
+      - name: "(a) libs present → gate passes"
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          OUT="$(mktemp)"
+          if bash scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh fx/with-libs.aab >"$OUT" 2>&1; then
+            cat "$OUT"
+          else
+            echo "::error::gate must PASS on a bundle WITH native libs (gh-798 AC3a) — regressed glob or layout assumption?"
+            cat "$OUT"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          grep -q "✅ 16 KB alignment check green" "$OUT" || {
+            echo "::error::gate passed without its green marker — verdict text drifted (gh-798 AC3a)"
+            exit 1
+          }
+
+      - name: "(b) libs absent → named failure, never a silent pass"
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          OUT="$(mktemp)"
+          if bash scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh fx/without-libs.aab >"$OUT" 2>&1; then
+            echo "::error::gate must FAIL on a bundle WITHOUT native libs (gh-798 AC3b) — native libs are expected in the store bundle"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          # Replay the output as PROOF of the named verdict — but strip the
+          # ::error:: command marker first, so the EXPECTED failure does not
+          # paint a red annotation onto this (green) run (gh-800 r2).
+          sed 's/::error::/[expected-failure proof, annotation stripped] /' "$OUT"
+          grep -q "expected native libs at base/lib/\*/\*\.so" "$OUT" || {
+            echo "::error::gate failed WITHOUT its named verdict — regressed to an inherited/unlabeled exit code (the exact gh-786 class)"
+            exit 1
+          }
+          echo "✅ self-test green: pass-on-libs + named-fail-without-libs verified"

uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: size-baselines-macos
          path: scripts/size_budget/*.tsv
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Package TestFlight PKG (arm64)
        if: matrix.arch == 'arm64'
        id: testflight_pkg
        env:
          MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_PASSWORD }}
          CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV: MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64
          CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV: MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_PASSWORD
          MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64:-}" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Mac Installer Distribution cert not configured — skipping TestFlight PKG (the DMG path is unaffected)."
            exit 0
          fi
          # gh-1865 model v3: the installer cert lives in the PERSISTENT
          # ci-signing keychain under its own label (idempotent install —
          # the old lazy keychain re-create + search-list re-assert here
          # was gh-1866 exposure #2). productbuild signs by the SHA-1
          # fingerprint, immune to same-subject name shadowing.
          ~/bin/ci-sign install fa-macos-installer
          INSTALLER_SHA1=$(~/bin/ci-sign sha1 fa-macos-installer)

          APP_PATH="flutter_app/build/macos/Build/Products/Release/Fa.app"
          PKG_NAME="fa-macos-arm64-${VERSION}.pkg"
          echo "Building TestFlight package: $APP_PATH → $PKG_NAME"
          productbuild --component "$APP_PATH" /Applications "$PKG_NAME" \
            --sign "$INSTALLER_SHA1"
          echo "pkg_name=$PKG_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Notarize DMG
        if: steps.signing.outputs.signed == 'true'
        env:
          MACOS_NOTARIZE_APPLE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_NOTARIZE_APPLE_ID }}
          MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID }}
          MACOS_NOTARIZE_APP_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_NOTARIZE_APP_PASSWORD }}
          DMG_NAME: ${{ steps.package.outputs.dmg_name }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$MACOS_NOTARIZE_APPLE_ID" ]; then
            echo "⚠️  Notarization secrets not set — skipping notarization"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "Submitting for notarization..."
          xcrun notarytool submit "$DMG_NAME" \
            --apple-id "$MACOS_NOTARIZE_APPLE_ID" \
            --team-id "$MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID" \
            --password "$MACOS_NOTARIZE_APP_PASSWORD" \
            --wait
          xcrun stapler staple "$DMG_NAME"
          echo "✅ Notarization complete"

      - name: Submit PKG to TestFlight
        if: steps.testflight_pkg.outputs.pkg_name != ''
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
          MACOS_PKG_PATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/${{ steps.testflight_pkg.outputs.pkg_name }}
          # External TestFlight distribution (issue #239): lanes fail
          # loudly when these are unset — set them once as repo variables.
          TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP: ${{ vars.TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP }}
          BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL: ${{ vars.BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL }}
          BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL: ${{ vars.BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL }}
          BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE: ${{ vars.BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE }}
          # gh-1522: the ASC/TestFlight version string rides the derived tag
          # version (store_pubspec_version prefers BUILD_NAME; the committed
          # pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder).
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT:-}" ]; then
            echo "::notice::App Store Connect API key not configured — skipping TestFlight upload (the PKG stays in artifacts)."
            exit 0
          fi
          bundle install
          bundle exec fastlane mac submit_only

      - name: Upload TestFlight PKG artifact
        if: steps.testflight_pkg.outputs.pkg_name != ''
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: fa-macos-testflight-pkg
          path: ${{ steps.testflight_pkg.outputs.pkg_name }}
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Upload macOS artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: Fa-macos-${{ matrix.arch }}
          path: |
            ${{ steps.package.outputs.dmg_name }}
            ${{ steps.package.outputs.zip_name }}
            ${{ steps.package.outputs.manifest_name }}
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Build and package no-sandbox release
        id: package_nosandbox
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          ARCH: ${{ matrix.arch }}
          # gh-2039: the point-of-use re-assert below re-imports the
          # identity if it is genuinely gone from the persistent
          # keychain — same env the provisioning step passes to ci-sign
          # (CI_SIGN_P12_* indirection), so the happy path stays a
          # millisecond re-verify and the degraded path self-heals.
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
          CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV: MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64
          CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV: MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD
          # gh-1865: SHA-1 pin instead of the name-based
          # MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID secret — build_macos_nosandbox.sh signs
          # via `codesign --sign "${identity}"` and falls back to ad-hoc
          # ("-") when unset, exactly like the old empty-secret path.
          FA_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.identity_sha1 }}
          FA_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM: ${{ secrets.MACOS_NOTARIZE_TEAM_ID }}
          PROFILE_UUID: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_uuid }}
          PROFILE_TEAM: ${{ steps.signing.outputs.profile_team }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cd flutter_app

So Nov 9's run (our ticket, gh-2075) failed specifically on the sqlite3 downloads across all three legs — a genuinely new failure mode, network-related, affecting all three download attempts in that window.

So the ticket's failure: the sqlite3 native-assets hook's build-time GitHub download failed on all three legs in the same window:
- Hosted CLI (macos-latest): 504 Gateway Time-out.
- Self-hosted arm64 (fa-m5-3) and x86_64 (fa-m5-2): wrong content with IDENTICAL hash `bef140a1a...` — a proxy/middlebox error page served with HTTP 200.

The Nov 8 arm64-only failure (size gate) is a DIFFERENT issue (probably a different ticket). Our ticket is gh-2075, run 42566734746 — the sqlite3 download failure.

Now, the fix decision. Options in repo-convention order:

The repo's established pattern for build-time downloads on these runners (WasmRun xcframework): a bounded retry loop with resume + digest verification, and where possible caching. For git mirrors: `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` with visible retries.

For sqlite3: the hook does a single GET with no retry. We can't change the hook, but we CAN:
1. **Pre-sed the hook's download cache before the build so the hook never needs the network** — but the cache location (`.dart_tool/hooks_runner/sqlite3/<input-hash>/shared/...`) is created during the build; pre-sed is fragile.

2. **Use user-defines `url_pattern` to point at a more reliable endpoint.** E.g., bypass the HTML→redirect chain? The `url_pattern` points at `https://github.com/.../releases/download/$RELEASE_TAG/$FILENAME` which 302s to `objects.githubusercontent.com`. We could substitute the DIRECT `https://objects.githubusercontent.com/...` — but those signed URLs expire; not viable.

4. **Retry the whole build step** — the app build step is ~15-25 min; a full retry is expensive but the matrix legs are serialized (2.5h budget). Meh.

KEY FINDING at line 425-427:

```dart
final outDirSharedUri = packageLayout.dartToolHooksRunner.resolve(
 'shared/${package.name}/${hook.name}/',
);
``

`outputDirectoryShared` = `<dartToolHooksRunner>/shared/sqlite3/build/` — a STABLE path, NOT per-input-hash! (`dartToolHooksRunner` is `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/` under the workspace root.) The per-input-hash dir (`16e357353/`) holds input.json/hook.dill, but the SHARED dir (where the sqlite3 download cache lives) is stable: `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/`.

So the sqlite3 hook's cache file is at:
`<workspace-root>/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/download-<hash8>/libsqlite3.dylib`

For flutter_app: `flutter_app/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/download-649fdf22/libsqlite3.dylib` (arm64) and `download-5b956194/libsqlite3.dylib` (x64).

If that file exists with the expected hash → hook reuses it, NO network needed. This is the hook's OWN documented cache ("Use a subdirectory of shared outputs to allow caching").

BUT — `flutter clean`... does it wipe `.dart_tool`? Yes, flutter clean deletes .dart_tool. And the build step does `flutter clean` at its start. So seeding must happen AFTER flutter clean, before/during the release build. The hook runs during `flutter build macos --release` (in the Flutter Asemble phase). A workflow pre-step between `--config-only` and `--release` can seed the cache:

```yaml
- name: Seed sqlite3 native-asset cache (retries)
 run: |
   # download libsqlite3.arm64.macos.dylib with retries →
   # flutter_app/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/download-649fdf22/libsqlite3.dylib
``

Hmm wait — but for `dart build cli` on the hosted runners, where does `dartToolHooksRunner` point? For a plain dart workspace: `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/` under the package root. `dart build cli` — the hook runs at build time; seeding before `dart build cli` works the same way: `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/download-<hash8>/libsqlite3.dylib` where hash8 = `38c4a60b` for 3.9.1 arm64.

Hold on — wait. There's a subtlety: the FILENAME inside the dir. `input.config.code.targetOS.libraryFileName(library.type.basename, DynamicLoadingBundled())` → for macOS: `libsqlite3.dylib`. Good.

And `library.dirname` = `download-${contentSha256Hash.substring(0, 8)}`.

So the exact cache path: `<root>/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/download-649fdf22/libsqlite3.dylib`.

Verification of hash: the hook re-hashes the file and reuses only on match — so a stale/wrong file fails SAFE (falls back to download), never ships wrong bytes. A seeded cache is integrity-neutral.

But there's still the question: what pins the hash8 values in the workflow? They come from the sqlite3 package version (3.7.0 for flutter_app, 3.9.1 for root). If pub resolution bumps sqlite3, the pinned dirs/URLs must move. The workflow must derive them dynamically rather than hard-code. Deriving from pubspec.lock + the package's asset_hashes.dart is doable but fiddly in bash.

Hmm, hmm. Wait. Let me reconsider — this is getting complex. Is seeding the cache too clever? Alternative: retry the failed download by retrying the BUILD only when the failure matches the sqlite3-download signature. That's a big hammer and wastes 20 min.

Actually — hmm, let me reconsider ANOTHER much simpler angle. The hook respects `HttpClient.findProxyFromEnvironment` and Dart 3.11+ passes proxy env vars to hooks. But that doesn't fix 504s.

OK here's the thing — let me look at this from the "what would the repo maintainer accept" angle:

The repo's existing precedent for exactly this problem class (build-time asset downloads on flaky networks, WasmRun.xcframework):
1. Bounded retry loop with `curl --fail -L -C -` + max-time per attempt.
2. Digest verification (sha256 pinned) — distinguishes corrupt/wrong content from complete.
3. Persistent partial for cross-run resume.
4. Cache (actions/cache) keyed by content.

The sqlite3 dylib download can use the SAME recipe, seeded into the hook's OWN cache directory (stable path, hash-keyed subdirs, hook re-validates hash → reuse-or-download fallback). This is the minimal, safe, convention-consistent fix:

- Add a small script `scripts/seed_sqlite3_native_assets.sh` (repo has a scripts/ dir with similar self-contained bash: build_fa_clip.sh, assert_macos_min_platform.sh, update_git_mirror.sh, prune_flutter_assets.sh) that:
 - takes the workspace root(s) + target arch(es);
 - resolves the installed sqlite3 version(s) + releaseTag + expected hash from the installed package's `lib/src/hook/asset_hashes.dart` (single source of truth — NO hard-coded hashes);
 - computes the shared cache dir `<root>/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/download-<hash8>/<libsqlite3.dylib>`;
 - skips if a hash-valid file is already there;
 - otherwise downloads with the WasmRun-style bounded retry loop (`curl --fail -L --max-time ...` × N) and verifies sha256 before placing;
 - on wrong content → purge and fail loud (like WasmRun's digest-purge).

- Wire it into build-macos.yml:
 - app legs: after `flutter build macos --config-only` + assert (the .dart_tool exists then; note flutter clean wipes it) and BEFORE `flutter build macos --release`.
 - CLI legs: after `dart pub get`, before `dart build cli`.

Wait — for the CLI leg on GitHub-hosted runners: does `dart pub get` create `.dart_tool`? Yes. And `dart build cli` reads the workspace at `.dart_tool`. The hook's shared dir would be created on demand; seeding creates it pre-emptively. 

Hmm, BUT: the CLI leg runs on macos-latest ARM64 AND macos-15-intel (x64). One arch per runner. The script can take an arch param.

For the app legs: matrix.arch arm64/x86_64 → arm64/x64 asset names. Both arches of dylib? Only the built arch is needed (FLUTER_XCODE_ARCHS=$ARCH, single-arch build).

Now — one more check: does the hook actually run with `dart build cli`? The CLI leg log shows "Running build hooks...Building assets for package:sqlite3 failed" during "Build CLI bundle" step — yes.

And does `dart build cli` re-run the hook if the shared cache file exists? The hook itself checks the file and reuses — but does hooks_runner SKIP running the hook entirely based on a cached output? There's `_runHookForPackageCached` — if the hook's OUTPUT is cached (output.json up-to-date), the hook may not even re-run; either way the previously-built asset is reused. Fine either way.

Edge: the hooks_runner id dir (`16e357353`) — that's where input.json lives; the shared dir is separate and stable. My earlier worry about the per-input-hash is resolved by line 425: `dartToolHooksRunner.resolve('shared/${package.name}/${hook.name}/')`.

content.thinking:
CONFIRMED:
- Per-build dir: `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/<package>/<checksum>/` (the `16e357353` in the log).
- SHARED dir: `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/` — stable under the workspace root's `.dart_tool`.

So the sqlite3 hook cache path is:
`<workspace-root>/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/download-<hash8>/libsqlite3.dylib`

Where hash8 = first 8 hex of the expected asset sha256 from the installed package's asset_hashes.dart. And the hook re-validates the hash on reuse — a wrong seeded file is never trusted (it falls back to download), so seeding is integrity-neutral.

One caveat: for a Flutter app, is the "workspace root" flutter_app (its own pubspec → its own .dart_tool)? #!/usr/bin/env bash
# build_fa_clip.sh — compile the native `fa-clip` pasteboard helper (gh-2040).
#
# Usage: build_fa_clip.sh [<output-path>]
#
# The helper rides the macOS CLI bundles (bundle/bin/fa-clip, per-arch —
# the release matrix builds each arch on a native runner, gh-2040 AC8) and
# installs beside the `fa` binary, which resolves it relative to its own
# executable path. Exit 0 = binary written; exit 1 = no toolchain (callers
# treat a missing helper as the named pasteboard-unavailable path, AC5).

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
SRC="$REPO_ROOT/tools/fa-clip/fa-clip.swift"
OUT="${1:-$REPO_ROOT/tools/fa-clip/fa-clip}"

if [ "$(uname -s)" != "Darwin" ]; then
  echo "fa-clip is macOS-only — not building on $(uname -s)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! command -v swiftc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "swiftc not found — fa-clip not built (paste degrades to the named unavailable path, gh-2040 AC5)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

case "$(uname -m)" in
  arm64) target="arm64-apple-macos10.13" ;;
  x86_64) target="x86_64-apple-macos10.13" ;;
  *) echo "unsupported arch for fa-clip: $(uname -m)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
swiftc -O -target "$target" -o "$OUT" "$SRC"
chmod +x "$OUT"
echo "built $OUT ($target)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  gh-1644 — update_git_mirror.sh self-test                                  ║
# ║  The contract closes the run-38855793382 incident ("Update local git      ║
# ║  mirrors" died exit 128 — "error: 2931 bytes of body are still            ║
# ║  expected"): the old inline workflow logic fetched ONCE (stderr            ║
# ║  swallowed), fell through to a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h       ║
# ║  transfer died mid-flight, and had no retry and no partial-dir cleanup.   ║
# ║  Scenarios (local file:// fixture remotes, fault-injected `git` shim):    ║
# ║    T1 fresh clone creates a working mirror                                ║
# ║    T2 fetch advances the mirror to new remote commits                     ║
# ║    T3 a poisoned partial mirror dir is recovered (recreate)               ║
# ║    T4 THE INCIDENT: transient fetch failure + armed clone failure —       ║
# ║        a fetch RETRY must recover with NO recreate (the legacy logic      ║
# ║        recreated, hit the failing clone and died exit 128)                ║
# ║    T5 persistent clone failure → nonzero exit after exactly               ║
# ║        MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS logged attempts, ::error marker, no          ║
# ║        partial dir left behind                                            ║
# ║    T6 a recreated mirror records the blob:none filter (gh-1477            ║
# ║        precedent — blobless mirror shrinks the flake window ~60 min→min)  ║
# ║    T7 fetch-retry exhaustion falls back to a successful recreate          ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh
# Legacy replay:      bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh --legacy
#   --legacy runs the incident scenarios against the PRE-FIX inline
#   workflow logic (embedded below, verbatim behavior of the old
#   build-macos.yml step): every scenario PASSES iff the legacy logic
#   FAILS the contract — i.e. the bug is reproduced. Zero legacy failures
#   means the repro is broken.

cd "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"   # repo root, any cwd
MODE="${1:-}"
SCRIPT="scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
if [ "$MODE" != "--legacy" ] && [ ! -f "$SCRIPT" ]; then
  echo "❌ $SCRIPT missing — run this selftest from the repo root" >&2
  exit 1
fi

WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
# Resolve the REAL git binary — NOT a PATH wrapper. This runner prepends a
# git-push-guard shim to PATH; exec-ing it from OUR shim would ping-pong
# (the wrapper re-resolves `git` via PATH back into the shim) and spin.
# `command -v -p` resolves against the system default PATH.
REAL_GIT="$(command -v -p git 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$REAL_GIT" ]; then REAL_GIT="$(command -v git)"; fi

pass=0
fail=0

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.

    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;
  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe
  their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, while nightly
  KEEPS running the file to produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.
  Flake intake consumes PR-dispatch runs only (gh-1537:
  `scripts/flake_watch.py` filters to `workflow_dispatch` events — the
  retired main trigger leaves SM validation dispatches and v* tag runs;
  a red tag run is a release-flow failure, triaged by daily-publish /
  ci-red-report, never quarantined as a flake). Dedup is per test name
  (the #1364 lesson): one test red across N runs files ONE issue.
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs
  pre-merge in ci.yml's `pty-visual` leg — gh-1538 retired the nightly
  duplicate — and on demand).

arguments.content:
## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The daily-publish `cli` leg (build-macos run 42566734746, 2026-11-09) failed all three macOS release jobs (Build macOS CLI arm64, Build macOS arm64, Build macOS x86_64) on the `package:sqlite3` native-assets build hook's single build-time download of the prebuilt `libsqlite3` dylib from GitHub releases.

**Root cause**: `sqlite3` (root CLI workspace: 3.9.1; `flutter_app`: 3.7.0) ships a native-assets build hook (`hook/build.dart` → `PrecompiledFromGithubAssets._fetchFromSource`) that downloads `https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases/download/<tag>/libsqlite3.<arch>.macos.dylib` with **one un-retried HTTP GET** during the build (`dart build cli` for the CLI bundle; the Flutter Assemble script phase for the macOS app). All three hook invocations in this run's window died on that request:
- Hosted CLI (macos-latest): `Unexpected response code: 504 Gateway Time-out` → `Running build hooks failed`, exit 255.
- Self-hosted app legs (fa-m5-2, fa-m5-3): the download returned HTTP 200 with **identical wrong bytes for both distinct arch assets** (sha256 `bef140a1a969…` for arm64 AND x64 — impossible for real binaries; a proxy/middlebox error page), caught by the hook's own digest pin: `Bad state: Hash of downloaded file … is bef140a1a…, expected 649fdf22… / 5b956194…` → `Target build_hooks failed` → `** BUILD FAILED **` ~20 min into each build.

Verification that this is transport, not upstream drift: post-incident fetches of all four assets (`sqlite3-3.7.0` arm64/x64, `sqlite3-3.9.1` arm64/x64) hash-match the package-pinned digests in each version's `lib/src/hook/asset_hashes.dart` exactly. The `SecTrustGetCertificateAtIndex` / `AVKeyValueStatus` deprecation warnings in the auto-filed signature are unrelated compiler noise; the `error: the following command failed with exit code 0` lines are Xcode's build-system noise as the overall build dies.

**Impact**: One flaky egress request kills three release legs (DMGs, CLI bundles, extension attach to the next tag); the release train and vpinned marker advance stall until the next green daily. The failure mode is recurring on this infrastructure (the fa-m5 egress path already needed the gh-1759 WasmRun retry recipe and the gh-1644 mirror retries for the same class).

**Fix approach**: The hook itself caches per content hash under the workspace's **stable** `<ws>/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/download-<hash8>/libsqlite3.dylib` path (`hooks_runner` resolves `shared/<package>/build/`, not per-input hashes) and **reuses an existing file only when its sha256 matches the package-pinned digest** (otherwise it re-downloads). So a seed script can install the pinned asset into that cache beforehand — integrity-neutral (wrong bytes are never trusted; the hook falls back to download), self-maintaining (version/tag/hashes are read from the installed package's own `asset_hashes.dart`, nothing pinned in the script), and it uses the repo's established download recipe (WasmRun/gh-1759: `curl --fail -L`, bounded attempts, per-attempt wall cap, sha256 verify before install, purge on mismatch). Wire it into build-macos.yml in exactly the three failing jobs — CLI legs after `dart pub get` / before `dart build cli`, app legs inside the build step after `--config-only` + min-platform gate (`.dart_tool` exists; `flutter clean` runs earlier in the same step) and before `--release`. Failures exit loud in seconds with remediation, never mid-build. Guard test pins the wiring (`test/ci_sqlite3_native_asset_seed_guard_test.dart`), selftest exercises the real script with a fault-injected curl shim (`scripts/seed_sqlite3_native_assets_selftest.sh`).

**Previous attempt**: none — first failure of this signature (the 2026-11-08 run 42496495862 failed on a different leg/step: the arm64 size-budget gate; its sqlite3 downloads succeeded).
